cards.text: Jesus and His companions head into Capernaum. It's the Sabbath, and right away Jesus walks into the synagogue and starts to teach. No warm-up, no small talk. Straight to it.

cards.question: Jesus is teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. How do the people react to His teaching?

cards.text: Mark tells us why: He taught “as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.” Me? I talk to my dough with authority every single morning, and it STILL does whatever it wants.
Then, suddenly, a man with an unclean spirit cries out right there in the synagogue. Friend, talk about interrupting the teacher.

cards.question: The unclean spirit cries out at Jesus in the synagogue. What does it call Him?
The unclean spirit has no idea who Jesus is.

cards.text: Jesus isn't having any of it. He rebukes the spirit.

cards.question: Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit in the synagogue. What does He command it?

answers.text: Be silent and come out of him
Tell Me your name right now

cards.text: The spirit throws the man into convulsions and comes out with a loud shriek. It leaves, but it does NOT leave quietly.

cards.question: All the people in the synagogue are amazed. They ask one another what this is. What do they call it?

answers.text: A sign from the old prophets

cards.question: The amazed people keep going: “He commands even the unclean ___, and they ___ Him!”

cards.text: Something like this doesn't stay inside one building. If they'd had group chats back then, this is the message EVERYBODY forwards.

cards.question: The news about Jesus starts to spread. How far does it go?

answers.text: Through the whole region of Galilee
Only around the town of Capernaum
All the way down into Egypt

cards.text: As soon as they leave the synagogue, Jesus and His companions head to the home of Simon and Andrew, the fishermen brothers He called to follow Him (Mark 1:16-18). James and John come along too.

cards.question: At Simon and Andrew's house, someone is sick in bed with a fever. Who is it?
They wait a few days before telling Jesus about Simon's sick mother-in-law.

cards.text: So Jesus goes to her. He takes her by the hand and helps her up.

cards.question: Jesus takes Simon's mother-in-law by the hand and helps her up. What happens to her fever?
With her fever gone, what does Simon's mother-in-law begin to do?

cards.text: Fever gone, and she's right up serving them. Me? I got ONE crumb stuck in my mustache once and needed the whole afternoon to recover.
That evening, after sunset, people bring Jesus all the sick and demon-possessed.

cards.question: That evening, people bring all the sick and demon-possessed to Jesus. Who gathers at the door?

cards.text: The WHOLE town at one front door. I get flustered when the oven timer and the doorbell go off at the same time. And Jesus heals many who are ill with various diseases and drives out many demons.

cards.question: Jesus drives out many demons that evening, but He won't let them speak. Why not?

answers.text: Because they knew who He was
Because the crowd was too loud
Because it was still the Sabbath

cards.text: Early in the morning, while it's still dark, Jesus gets up and goes out to a solitary place. Me? Before sunrise, I'm hitting snooze and negotiating with my own mustache.

cards.question: Early in the morning, while it's still dark, Jesus goes out to a solitary place to ___.

cards.text: Simon and his companions go looking for Him. Friend, I can't even find my apron in the morning, and it's TIED ON ME.

cards.question: When Simon and his companions find Jesus in the solitary place, what do they tell Him?

answers.text: The scribes want to see You

cards.text: Everyone is looking for Him. You'd think He'd head right back to the crowd. But Jesus answers them.

cards.question: Simon and his companions say everyone is looking for Jesus. What does Jesus say they should do?

answers.text: Go on to the neighboring towns to preach
Go back to Capernaum to heal everyone
Stay in this quiet place to pray longer

cards.question: Jesus says preaching in the neighboring towns is why He has come.

cards.text: So He goes throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons. One town was never going to be big enough.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "He commands even the unclean ___, and they ___ Him!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Jesus and His companions head into Capernaum. It's the Sabbath, and right away Jesus walks into the synagogue and starts to teach. No warm-up, no small talk. Straight to it."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: James and John appear for the first time in this lesson with no word on who they are. Simon and Andrew get a description, but the card only says "James and John come along too."

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card only repeats Mark 1:31 (fever gone, she serves them), which cards 4 to 6 already covered, and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: a recap of the crowd, a joke, and the healings in Mark 1:34.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup line "You'd think He'd head right back to the crowd. But Jesus answers them." tells the baker that Jesus won't go back. That rules out the wrong answer "Go back to Capernaum to heal everyone" on card 17. The card's first sentence also just repeats card 15's answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: In Mark 1:38, Jesus says "so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come." The text doesn't spell out exactly what "that" points to. The statement narrows it to "preaching in the neighboring towns."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
